newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot to replace Ilyushin cargo fleet.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot to replace Ilyushin cargo fleet.

text.p: Russia's flagship carrier Aeroflot -Russian International Airlines plans to replace its entire cargo fleet of Ilyushin Il-76s by the turn of the century, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
He said that 16 Ilyushins, the only planes that Aeroflot cargo owns, must be retired over 1997-1999.
"These planes fly on scheduled cargo routes between Southeast Asia and Western Europe via Moscow...but it is extremely inefficient for us because they are outdated," he said.
Aeroflot cargo leases Russian-made Antonov-124s and a single McDonnel-Douglas DC-10-30. The spokesman said Aeroflot planned soon to lease a second DC-10-30.
"The first such aircraft, which we have operated for two years, shows good results on the Seoul-Moscow-Frankfurt route," he said.
Aeroflot also plans to lease Airbus Industries A-310 cargo planes or Russian-made Tupolev-204 freighters, he said, but did not give more details.
Aeroflot leases 13 Western-made planes, including 12 passenger jets and the DC-10 freighter.
Last year the carrier made a firm order for three Russian-made Ilyushin Il-96T cargo planes powered by U.S.-made Pratt & Whitney engines and Collins avionics, for delivery in 1997-98.
